title: keel runtime descriptor
description: A runtime descriptor, runtimes/<id>.yaml: the data that drives dispatch for one runtime. It covers the binary and its Windows resolution, prompt and submit channels, the schema flag, modes with execution class and rung, argv template, stream parser, session handling, budget flags, exit codes, env scrub control, the names-only provider path set, permission generation, trust, hooks and the verify-by-probe list. Every unverified fact carries verification_status. Values (endpoints, keys, model names) never appear: native provider variable names appear only in provider.native_env.

kind.description: cli: an external agent CLI; direct: keel's own tool-less direct-lane child process (M6).

verification_status.description: Status of the descriptor as a whole; unverified until the doctor probes pass.

tested_version.description: Version the descriptor was written against, or null when the runtime was not available.

git_required.description: Whether the runtime needs a git checkout as its working directory.

instruction_files.description: Instruction files the runtime reads natively, for example AGENTS.md.

dirs.description: Directories the runtime is probed to scan for skills; keel copies skills only there.

agent_files.description: keel-owned agent files for this runtime, if it can select them.

schema_flag_takes.description: inline: minified JSON as the argv value (Claude Code); path: a schema file path (Codex --output-schema, Qwen Code @path); null: no schema flag.

argv_template.description: Argument tokens with {placeholders} the Steward fills. Never a value, URL, key or model name.

parser.description: Stream parser id that normalizes output to canonical run events.

cwd.description: Working directory of the child: normally the task or verify worktree; the run directory is added with --add-dir or --include-directories.

env_toggles.description: Runtime toggles keel sets in the child environment, for example the per-run config path. Their values are keel-owned; a provider value never appears.

auth_argv.description: Argument tokens spliced at {auth_argv}, per auth mode of the routing profile. A mode that is not listed splices nothing.

bypass_equivalent.description: True when the only headless mode behaves like a permission bypass (Kimi Code -p); such a runtime stays at rung D for writing seats until a non-bypass write mode is verified by probe.

control_plane_exposure.description: Expected exposure of .git/keel to this runtime's tools on native Windows.

capability_probes.description: The verify-by-probe list: doctor probes that move a fact from documented or probed to verified.

name.description: Bare command name resolved on PATH, or null for the direct lane.

windows_resolution.description: How the Windows launcher is resolved: npm .cmd/.ps1 shims are resolved to the node script they wrap; spawn never goes through a shell.

shell.description: Always false: keel never spawns with shell:true (CVE-2024-27980).

promptChannel.description: How the brief reaches the child. The same brief bytes go through every channel.

kind.description: argv is allowed only for a fixed short string, because of the Windows 8191/32767 command-line limits.

fixed_prompt.description: The fixed short instruction passed with -p or as the positional message; never the brief itself.

flag.description: Flag that carries a prompt file path, for example --append-system-prompt-file.

schema_flag.description: Flag that takes the output schema, for example --json-schema or --output-schema.

output_flag.description: Flag that writes the final message to a file, if any.

mode.description: A permission mode. The rung is chosen per runtime and mode from probes.

id.description: Mode id, for example plan, accept-edits, read-only or workspace-write.

argv.description: Mode-specific flags; bypass flags are never generated.

submit_channel.description: The result channel of this mode; read-only modes use the final message or MCP. The ACK channel per mode is tabulated in docs/02-alignment.md.

rung.description: The rung this mode reaches, chosen from probes; null only for the direct lane, which has no tools or hooks and sits outside the A-D ladder.

value.description: A keel-owned value, which may use argv placeholders such as {run_dir}.

argv.description: Tokens for this auth mode; they name profiles and flags, never a value.

resume.description: Argument tokens to resume a session.

fork.description: Argument tokens to fork a session.

posix_only.description: True for signal-derived codes such as 143, interpreted on POSIX only.

control.description: How subprocess environment scrubbing is controlled (a flag, setting or variable name); never a value.

provider.description: Provider compatibility and the in-memory name mapping. The only place native provider variable names appear.

protocols.description: Protocols compatible at resolve time; an incompatible route is blocked(runtime_unavailable).

native_env.description: In-memory mapping from the routed profile's named variables to the runtime's native names.

adapters.description: Optional. Per protocol, the adapter package a per-run config names (opencode: the AI SDK provider package) and the suffix appended to the base URL reference; names only, never a value.

package.description: Adapter package name, for example an npm package the runtime loads.

base_url_suffix.description: Appended to the base URL reference in the per-run config, for example /v1 when the adapter expects the version segment and the protocol convention omits it (docs/10-providers.md section 5); empty when none.

from.description: Which named profile variable supplies the value.

name.description: Native variable name the runtime reads, for example ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.

providerPathSet.description: The names-only provider path set. keel stats these paths (PRESENT/ABSENT) and never opens them; ingest fails a run on any tool event touching them.

home_env.description: Names of variables that point at runtime homes, for example CODEX_HOME.

paths.description: Runtime credential and configuration locations as strings, for example ~/.codex/auth.json. keel only stats them.

dotenv.description: Whether .env* files belong to the set.

mechanism.description: How keel provisions permissions for a headless run; shared settings files are never written.

deny_read.description: Whether keel generates deny-read rules for the provider path set.

never_generate.description: Flags keel never generates, for example permission-bypass flags.

project_layers.description: When project-level runtime configuration loads. keel never relies on project layers for enforcement.

override_flags.description: Trust flags used only after a Board --rule override.

hooks.description: Hook delivery; the canonical event table is runtimes/hook-events.yaml.

delivery.description: How keel hooks reach the runtime. Hooks warn and gates decide: every hook fails open and is journaled.

blocking_exit_code.description: Exit code that blocks, if the runtime supports blocking hooks.

claim.description: The fact to verify by probe.
